title: God as Root Axiom

canonical_node.axiom: The Trinitarian God is the irreducible root axiom of the framework; all other claims derive from this through formal grammar constrained by physics.
definitions: God: The Trinitarian God, three persons in one being, each constituted through the others, none prior, none derived, none reducible.
Perichoresis: Mutual indwelling; the persons ARE their relations.
Love: The ground state of the coupling between the persons.
Physics: The ordered created medium where relation, consequence, choice, time, repair, embodiment, and love can become publicly meaningful.
Grace: God's unmerited favor, entering creation from beyond the closed system.
Agency: The capacity of creatures to choose, including the ability to refuse.
derivation: Every formal system has a foundational axiom that cannot be proven within the system.
This framework adopts God as its single root axiom.
From the Trinity, four fundamental debts are paid: Existence (aseity), Distinction (persons), Relation (perichoresis), Orientation (love).
Physics is the created medium that enables meaningful love, choice, and redemption.
The properties of physical laws are read as analogical portraits of divine attributes.
The narrative maps (Descent, Progressive Revelation) derive from the axiom through logical steps.
The necessary ground argument derives five required properties of the source of coherence from mathematical proofs.
canonical_node.action: The system should treat God as the irreducible root axiom, use the Trinity to ground existence, distinction, relation, and orientation, and interpret physics as the created medium for love and redemption, while maintaining the distinction between physics and grace.
boundary: This axiom does not claim to prove God's existence; it asserts God as the unprovable ground.
It does not equate physics with grace; physics describes conditions, not grace itself.
It does not claim that the analogical mappings are proof; they are declared bridges.
It does not claim that the framework can be fully formalized; it acknowledges partial formalization.
test: Check that all derivations trace back to the God axiom without circularity.
Verify that the four debts (existence, distinction, relation, orientation) are consistently grounded in the Trinity.
Ensure that physics is not used to prove God but as a medium consistent with the axiom.
Test the analogical mappings for internal consistency and note that they are not proofs.
Check that the framework names its own kill conditions and remains falsifiable in principle.

dg1_dependencies: None; this is the root axiom and depends on nothing else.
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a single irreducible foundation that grounds existence, distinction, relation, and orientation, and offers a coherent narrative framework for interpreting physics and theology.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the requirement that every formal system has an unprovable axiom; it does not attempt to prove God.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If removed, the entire framework loses its foundational grounding; no other axiom can substitute without changing the system's identity.

classification.claim_class: Theological axiom with analogical bridges to physics
classification.recommended_atom_action: Preserve as a foundational axiom; treat analogical mappings as declared bridges, not proofs; require further formalization and adversarial testing.

overstatement_risks: Claiming that physics proves God's character when it only provides analogies.
Treating the necessary ground argument as a proof of God's existence when it is a philosophical argument.
Overstating the convergence of evidence as definitive proof.
Confusing the unprovability of the axiom with evidence for its truth.
kill_conditions: If a physical law is found whose properties do not match any spiritual pattern, the analogical mapping fails.
If the necessary ground argument is shown to be logically invalid.
If the framework claims to prove God's existence, it violates its own axiom.
risk.lean_target: Axiom: God as root; physics as created medium; analogies as declared bridges.

plain_summary: This document establishes God as the single root axiom of the framework, grounding existence, distinction, relation, and orientation through the Trinity. It interprets physics as the created medium for love and redemption, and draws analogies between physical laws and divine attributes. The document explicitly states that these are analogies, not proofs, and that the axiom itself is unprovable. It includes narrative maps and a method for cross-resolution testing. The overall status is coherent as a theological framework, but the scientific and mathematical claims are not established as proofs.
